question:
Let G = (V, E) be a finite directed acyclic graph with |E| > 0. Which of the following must be true?
I. G has a vertex with no incoming edge.
II. G has a vertex with no outgoing edge.
III. G has an isolated vertex, that is, one with neither an incoming edge nor an outgoing edge.
options: I and III only
None of the above
I and II only
II and III only
I, II, and a vertex with one outgoing edge
I, II, and a vertex with one incoming edge
All of the above (I, II, III)
II only
I only
III only
model_outputs:
An undirected graph is called a DAG (directed acyclic graph), meaning that any path between two vertices contains exactly one edge. In a DAG, every node except possibly the root has outdegree 1 (it has one incoming edge) and indegree 1 (it has one outgoing edge).

For a DAG G = (V, E), let V' denote the set of nodes with indegree 0 (i.e., no outgoing edges), and let V'' denote the set of nodes with outdegree 0 (no incoming edges). Then V' ∪ V'' = V.

Option I is false, since we could have a vertex with no incoming edges but still have an outgoing edge.

Option II is also false, since we could have a vertex with no incoming edges and still have an incoming edge.

Option III is true, since if a vertex has no incoming edges, it cannot have any other incoming edges either, and thus has no incoming edges.

Therefore, the answer is (C).
